title: The South Pole
summary: Five Norwegians with dogs and skis race a British expedition to the last great blank on the map. They find a new way up through the mountains and reach the Pole on 14 December 1911.
sourceNote: Amundsen's own account, The South Pole, appeared in English in 1912, written up from his diary. Positions on the polar journey come from his sun sights, which later checks found to be good.

knownWorld.note: Approximate, hand-drawn: the world on the charts of 1910. Antarctica was known only at its edges, along the Ross Sea and the Ice Barrier, and along Shackleton's route up the Beardmore Glacier to 88°23′ south.

moments.title: The Bay of Whales
moments.text: The Fram anchors in an inlet of the Ice Barrier that Shackleton had thought too unstable to winter on. Amundsen, reading the old charts, judges that it has not moved in seventy years, and builds his hut on the ice itself.

moments.title: Depots
moments.text: Before winter they haul food south and cache it in depots at 80, 81 and 82 degrees, marking each with a line of flags across the route so it can be found in fog.

moments.title: The polar night
moments.text: The sun sets for four months. In the hut and tunnels dug into the snow, the men refit sledges, make lighter equipment and plan.

moments.title: The false start
moments.text: Too eager to beat Scott, they set out with the cold still near minus fifty. Dogs freeze, men's heels are frostbitten, and they retreat in disorder. Hjalmar Johansen's open anger at the retreat splits the party.

moments.title: Five men
moments.text: Amundsen, Olav Bjaaland, Helmer Hanssen, Sverre Hassel and Oscar Wisting leave for the Pole with four sledges and fifty-two dogs.

moments.title: Mountains
moments.text: A great range rises on the horizon to the south, peak behind peak, where no map shows anything. Amundsen names it for Queen Maud.

moments.title: The Axel Heiberg Glacier
moments.text: Instead of Shackleton's route, far to the west, they look for their own way up. A steep, broken glacier climbs nearly 3,000 metres to the plateau in four days.

moments.title: The Butcher's Shop
moments.text: At the top, as planned from the start, they kill twenty-four of the dogs to feed the rest and themselves. Amundsen writes that the camp's name was well earned.

moments.title: Farther than anyone
moments.text: They pass 88° 23′, Shackleton's farthest south, and the Norwegian flag goes up on the leading sledge.

moments.title: The Pole
moments.text: In the afternoon the sledge-meters show the distance run. All five hands hold the flag as it is planted. They call the plateau King Haakon VII's Plateau, and before leaving set up a tent with a letter for Scott.

moments.title: Back to Framheim
moments.text: After more than three months on the ice, the five come back to the hut early in the morning, with eleven of the dogs, all in good health.

moments.title: Hobart
moments.text: From Tasmania Amundsen cables the news to the world. Scott's party had reached the Pole five weeks after him; none of the five survived the journey back.
